newsitem.title: USA: Ga. bill would exempt hotels from school tax - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ga. bill would exempt hotels from school tax - paper.

text.p: The Georgia House has passed a proposal exempting hotel bills from the one-cent sales tax for schools that was just approved by one-third of the state's school districts, the Atlanta-Journal Constitution said Thursday.

The author of the bill, Rep. Mike Polak, D-DeKalb, said the proposal was designed to protect Atlanta's tourism industry. If the local-option sales tax increase is applied to hotel bills, it would raise total hotel taxes in Atlanta to 14 percent, the second highest rate in the nation.
Chicago's hotel tax is 14.9 percent, while most major cities in the Southeast charge 11 percent to 12 percent.
If passed in the Senate, Polak's bill would cap hotel taxes in Georgia at 13 percent. The state collects seven percent, so local governments would not be allowed to collect more than six percent.

Georgia voters approved a constitutional amendment in November allowing school districts to levy a one-cent local option sales tax increase for up to five years to pay for school construction and early debt retirement.
Sixty-nine of the state's 180 school districts rushed to put the proposals on the ballot on Tuesday, and 65 of the proposals passed, including those in all 11 Atlanta-area school districts.
